verses.1: During his reign, Nebuchadnezzar became king of Babylon. Yehoyakim served him for three years before he rebelled against him.
verses.2: And Jehovah sent forth the armies of Cush, as well as the armies of Aram. He also sent forth the armies of Moab and the armies of the children of Ammon. They were sent into Judah to destroy it, according to what Jehovah had commanded through His prophets.
verses.3: But by the Lord’s will, in Judah there would be no more sin on their faces, as for all the evil that they had done.
verses.4: And also, the blood that was spilled and filled Jerusalem with pure blood. But Jehovah did not accept it as a sacrifice.
verses.5: And all the words of Jehoyakim, and everything he did, are written in the book of the days of the kings of Judah.
verses.6: And Jehoiakim lay down with his fathers. And Jehoiakim’s son became king in his place.
verses.7: And the king of Egypt did not go away from his land anymore. For the king of Babylon took away everything that belonged to the king of Egypt, right up to the river Euphrates.
verses.8: Ben-Shemona ruled for twelve years. Then, three months after him, he became king in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Nehushta, daughter of Elanatan from Jerusalem.
verses.9: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father had done.
verses.10: On that day, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem. The city was taken captive.
verses.11: And Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came upon the city. His servants also oppressed the people of that city.
verses.12: And Jehoiachin, the king of Judah, went up against King Babylon. He took him along with his mother, his servants, his officers, and his guards. He captured King Babylon in the year 597.
verses.13: And he took out all the treasures from the house of the LORD and from the palace of the king. He also took out all the gold objects that Solomon, the king of Israel, had made in the house of the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded.
verses.14: And he destroyed all of Jerusalem, along with all its people and all the rulers of the army. He killed twelve thousand men, and all the fugitives and those who were trapped were not spared from destruction. Not a single person survived among the people of the land.
verses.15: And he destroyed Jerusalem along with the king’s mother, all of the king’s women, and all of his servants. He also destroyed all the cattle in the land.
verses.16: And all the soldiers: seven thousand, and the scribes, and one thousand who were prisoners. All of them were warriors. They were brought by King Babylon from all over the land.
verses.17: And King Babylon ruled over Mataniah, his father. He took his name as “Tzadkiel”.
verses.18: He reigned for forty-one years as king. He ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mother’s name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremias from Libnah.
verses.19: And he did evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Yehoyakim had done.
verses.20: For on account of Jehovah’s anger, they remained in Jerusalem and Judea until he cast them from his presence. And Zadokiah rebelled against King Babylon.
